g.text: From authoritative source to trusted, queryable knowledge
Seven stages. The green-bordered components are the four services I implemented; everything else is marked for what it actually is.
four separate trust answers, never one

svg.text: WHAT IS MINE, AND WHAT IS NOT

g.text: Preprocessor · Loader · Health Service · Dashboard — four of the
Entity Producer — it predates legal ingestion; I added EU/CELLAR
PostgreSQL, Qdrant, Neo4j, MinIO, Kafka, the legal chatbot —
The publishers themselves. Outside the system entirely.

This was not a chatbot over documents. The engineering problem was turning changing, heterogeneous authoritative information into structured, searchable, verifiable machine knowledge while preserving provenance — and giving operators control over ingestion, validation and lifecycle state. Most of the
difficulty was in the second half of that sentence.
One rule makes it debuggable: four stores, one writer each. That is why ‘which service made this row wrong?’ always has exactly one answer.
